name: Canada
summary_text: Canada is exceptionally safe for trans visitors — the strongest of the large Western countries. Gender identity and expression are protected grounds in the Canadian Human Rights Act and the Criminal Code's hate-crime provisions (Bill C-16, 2017); most provinces offer self-declaration legal gender recognition; federal documents offer an X marker; and healthcare coverage is universal. There are no bathroom laws, no border friction (Canadian authorities have not issued or received trans-traveler warnings), and courts consistently enforce protections. The counterweights are real but climate-level: police-reported hate crimes have risen six consecutive years (+169% since 2018), with gender identity/expression crimes among the fastest-growing categories; Egale documents a rising organised anti-trans movement; and Alberta/Saskatchewan have enacted resident-facing policy rollbacks (school pronoun and healthcare restrictions). A 2022 federal survey found 39% of 2SLGBTQI+ respondents experienced identity-based violence in five years — 90% of it verbal abuse, 17% physical. For a visitor: full legal protection, functioning recourse, low probability of anything beyond verbal harassment in hostile pockets.

sources.title: The Daily — Police-reported hate crime in Canada, 2024
sources.claim_summary: Statistics Canada (March 2026): police-reported hate crime in 2024 was relatively stable (4,882 incidents, +1%) after a 34% jump 2022-2023; incidents targeting sexual orientation fell 26% to 658; overall hate crime has more than doubled since 2018.

Egale Canada UPR submission (2012): overview of LGBT human rights in Canada - sexual orientation in the Charter since 1995, marriage equality 2005; but trans protections limited and varying by jurisdiction, with no federal gender-identity discrimination law at the time; identifies gaps against the Yogyakarta Principles.

sources.title: P.E.I. transgender community applauds ID changes | CBC News
sources.claim_summary: CBC News (April 2016): P.E.I. moved to make it easier for trans people to change gender on official documents - the Vital Statistics Act amendment requires only a declaration of identified gender plus a doctor's letter, removing the surgery requirement; welcomed by the trans community.

sources.title: With gender identity bill, Canada shows leadership in advancing human rights - The Globe and Mail
sources.claim_summary: The Globe and Mail (June 2017): Canada's Senate passed Bill C-16 (67-11), prohibiting discrimination based on gender identity and expression - framed as Canadian leadership amid global backlash; contrasts with anti-LGBT violence elsewhere.

Ontario Human Rights Commission policy on discrimination because of sexual orientation: the legal context, case law and legislation under the Ontario Human Rights Code (which also covers gender identity and gender expression) - official provincial human-rights framework.
